q: A 78-year-old woman with advanced dementia is bedbound and cannot change position without help. She also has urinary incontinence and reduced food intake. Which factor does Hazzard identify as the most important risk factor for pressure injury?
o: Persistent moisture exposure from urinary incontinence
Severely restricted mobility and inability to reposition
Poor nutrition that reduces padding over bony prominences
Sensory loss that reduces protective responses to pressure
explanation:
Tissue is most vulnerable when compression over a bony prominence goes uninterrupted. Other risks can reduce its tolerance to that load.

**Severely restricted mobility is the principal risk.** She cannot make the spontaneous movements that unload the sacrum or heels, so pressure persists until someone helps her turn.

**A. Incontinence-related moisture.** Wet skin is more susceptible to shear and superficial damage. It increases risk alongside immobility.
**B. Inability to reposition.** This directly prolongs loading at the same site and is the strongest risk factor across patient populations.
**C. Poor nutrition.** Loss of cushioning and inadequate intake reduce tolerance and impair repair. They do not explain the duration of uninterrupted pressure.
**D. Sensory loss.** It reduces the warning that normally prompts movement. The patient already cannot move off the pressure even with assistance cues.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 681–683.

optionRationales.body: . Incontinence-related moisture.** Wet skin is more susceptible to shear and superficial damage. It increases risk alongside immobility.
. Inability to reposition.** This directly prolongs loading at the same site and is the strongest risk factor across patient populations.
. Poor nutrition.** Loss of cushioning and inadequate intake reduce tolerance and impair repair. They do not explain the duration of uninterrupted pressure.
. Sensory loss.** It reduces the warning that normally prompts movement. The patient already cannot move off the pressure even with assistance cues.

**Severely restricted mobility is the principal risk.** She cannot make the spontaneous movements that unload the sacrum or heels, so pressure persists until someone helps her turn.

q: A 78-year-old woman hospitalized with a COPD exacerbation is to receive antibiotics. She has comorbidities and recent antibiotic exposure. Which principle should guide antibiotic selection according to Hazzard?
o: Treat sputum culture as a reliable way to distinguish colonization from infection
Use sputum volume as sufficient information for choosing the antibiotic spectrum
Consider disease severity, comorbidities, interactions, and local resistance patterns
Treat prior facility exposure and severe obstruction as evidence of lower resistance risk
explanation:
An exacerbation can follow viral infection, bacterial infection or both. Once antibiotics are indicated, choose a regimen likely to cover the pathogens this patient carries.
**Weigh severity, comorbidities, drug interactions, recent antibiotic exposure and local resistance.**

**A. Rely on a positive sputum culture.** Airway colonization can produce a positive culture between exacerbations. A culture is more informative after treatment failure or with resistant-organism risk.
**B. Choose coverage by sputum volume.** A change in sputum helps characterize the episode but cannot identify an organism or its susceptibility.
**C. Individualize the spectrum.** Her recent treatment can select resistant organisms, and her other illnesses and drugs affect which antibiotic she can tolerate.
**D. Interpret facility exposure as reassuring.** Recent acute or subacute care and severe obstruction increase the likelihood of resistant organisms.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1260–1261.
ref: Hazzard Ch 81 — CHRONIC OBSTRUCTIVE PULMONARY DISEASE

optionRationales.body: . Rely on a positive sputum culture.** Airway colonization can produce a positive culture between exacerbations. A culture is more informative after treatment failure or with resistant-organism risk.
. Choose coverage by sputum volume.** A change in sputum helps characterize the episode but cannot identify an organism or its susceptibility.
. Individualize the spectrum.** Her recent treatment can select resistant organisms, and her other illnesses and drugs affect which antibiotic she can tolerate.
. Interpret facility exposure as reassuring.** Recent acute or subacute care and severe obstruction increase the likelihood of resistant organisms.

explanationParts.text:
An exacerbation can follow viral infection, bacterial infection or both. Once antibiotics are indicated, choose a regimen likely to cover the pathogens this patient carries.
**Weigh severity, comorbidities, drug interactions, recent antibiotic exposure and local resistance.**

q: בהכנת תעודת רופא לצורך בקשה למינוי אפוטרופוס למטופל עם דמנציה ושינוי קוגניטיבי חריף, איזה תוכן נדרש בחוזר מעבר לתיאור מחלות הרקע?
o: העדפת המשפחה למוסד ומידת זמינותו לקליטה
הערכת קוגניציה ותובנה ומשך מינוי
עלות השהייה במוסד ומקור המימון האפשרי
ציון גיל המטופל ומספר האבחנות שברשימתו
explanation:
בחוות דעת על צורך במינוי בעקבות פגיעה קוגניטיבית מתארים יכולת הבנה ותובנה בנוגע לעניין, סיכוי לשיפור והתקופה הנחוצה. **הערכת קוגניציה ותובנה ומשך מינוי**.

**א. העדפת המשפחה למוסד ומידת זמינותו לקליטה.** העדפה מוסדית אינה הערכת כשרות.
**ב. הערכת קוגניציה ותובנה ומשך מינוי.** הערכת הקוגניציה והתובנה תומכת בקביעה אם יש צורך זמני או ממושך.
**ג. עלות השהייה במוסד ומקור המימון האפשרי.** עלות האשפוז אינה תחליף להערכה רפואית.
**ד. ציון גיל המטופל ומספר האבחנות שברשימתו.** גיל ומספר אבחנות אינם מתארים את יכולת ההחלטה.

q: A 73-year-old man is evaluated for delusions and hallucinations. After medical evaluation and medication review, the decision is made to start an antipsychotic. There is no immediate danger requiring urgent sedation. Compared with a younger patient, what starting-dose and titration approach is recommended?
o: Use the usual younger-adult starting dose and titrate slowly according to response
Use the usual younger-adult starting dose and titrate rapidly according to response
Use a lower starting dose than in a younger adult and titrate rapidly according to response
Use a lower starting dose than in a younger adult and titrate slowly according to response
explanation:
When antipsychotic treatment is warranted in an older adult without a need for rapid sedation, **start at a lower dose and titrate slowly**. Reassess the target symptom, orthostatic pressure, alertness and motor adverse effects.

**A. Usual adult dose, slow titration.** The starting exposure may already be excessive for a sensitive older patient.
**B. Usual adult dose, rapid escalation.** Both choices increase the risk of early toxicity.
**C. Low dose, rapid escalation.** Fast increases can cause adverse effects before response to the previous dose can be assessed.
**D. Low dose, slow titration.** Small adjustments guided by response help identify the lowest effective dose.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1028.
ref: Hazzard Ch 66 — GENERAL TOPICS IN GERIATRIC PSYCHIATRY

optionRationales.body: . Usual adult dose, slow titration.** The starting exposure may already be excessive for a sensitive older patient.
. Usual adult dose, rapid escalation.** Both choices increase the risk of early toxicity.
. Low dose, rapid escalation.** Fast increases can cause adverse effects before response to the previous dose can be assessed.
. Low dose, slow titration.** Small adjustments guided by response help identify the lowest effective dose.

explanationParts.text: When antipsychotic treatment is warranted in an older adult without a need for rapid sedation, **start at a lower dose and titrate slowly**. Reassess the target symptom, orthostatic pressure, alertness and motor adverse effects.

q: A 77-year-old woman with permanent primary hypothyroidism and ischemic heart disease is starting hormone replacement. Which approach to levothyroxine treatment is appropriate at her age?
o: Titrate levothyroxine cautiously toward a TSH near the upper normal limit
Titrate levothyroxine cautiously toward a suppressed TSH below the normal range
Replace levothyroxine with T3 to provide more physiologic hormone replacement
Stop levothyroxine after TSH normalizes to complete the cure of hypothyroidism
explanation:
Levothyroxine replaces the T4 a failing thyroid cannot supply. In an older adult with ischemic heart disease, **start cautiously and titrate toward the upper normal TSH range**.

**A. Cautious titration and upper-normal TSH** This allows adequate replacement while avoiding excess thyroid stimulation of the heart. Wait for a stable response before increasing again.
**B. Cautious titration to suppressed TSH** Deliberate suppression would create a risk of atrial fibrillation and bone loss during routine replacement.
**C. Replace T4 with T3** Tissues produce T3 from T4 as needed. Taking T3 can produce excessive levels and cardiac effects.
**D. Stop after normalization** A normal TSH shows the replacement dose is working. Permanent failure generally requires lifelong treatment.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1552, Management of hypothyroidism.

. Cautious titration to suppressed TSH** Deliberate suppression would create a risk of atrial fibrillation and bone loss during routine replacement.
. Replace T4 with T3** Tissues produce T3 from T4 as needed. Taking T3 can produce excessive levels and cardiac effects.
. Stop after normalization** A normal TSH shows the replacement dose is working. Permanent failure generally requires lifelong treatment.

q:
בן 79, הגיע מחוסר הכרה למיון. Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) = 4. בבדיקתו כעת פוקח עיניים בתגובה לקריאת שמו, בבדיקת אישונים מגיבים לאור, מבולבל, עונה לא לעניין, מושיט יד לכיוון הכאב. ה- GCS כעת 12.
איזה מהממצאים בבדיקתו לא השפיע על העלייה ב- GCS?
o: תגובת אישונים לאור
תגובה מילולית
תגובה מוטורית לכאב
פתיחת עיניים לגירוי
keySource: IMA 2026-Jun Basic official answer key after appeals, Q150
chapterTitle: Harrison 22e ch. 311 – Approach to the Patient with Critical Illness
explanation:
The standard Glasgow Coma Scale adds eye opening, verbal response and motor response. **Pupillary light reactivity does not contribute to the standard GCS total**, although it remains an important part of the neurologic examination.

**A. Pupillary response.** Record it separately. Pupillary reaction is incorporated into some prognostic extensions but not the original three-component score.
**B. Verbal response.** Confused conversation scores four, and inappropriate words score three. Characterize the actual response.
**C. Motor response.** Moving the hand toward the painful stimulus indicates localization and scores five.
**D. Eye opening.** Opening the eyes on hearing his name scores three. Eye opening, motor localization and confused conversation can together give the stated total of 12.

Reference · Harrison 22e, p. 2292.

. Eye opening.** Opening the eyes on hearing his name scores three. Eye opening, motor localization and confused conversation can together give the stated total of 12.

q:
בן 82, עצמאי בתפקודו ושמור קוגניטיבית, בריא בדרך כלל ולא מעשן. סובל בחודשים האחרונים מאירועים של לחץ בחזה, המתרחש לאחר מאמץ גופני, ומוקל מיד במנוחה. הכאב מופיע בעליה של 3 קומות במדרגות או הליכה של 10 דקות. אק"ג במנוחה ללא ממצא חריג.

explanation:
Predictable chest pressure brought on by exertion and relieved by rest suggests stable angina. A normal resting ECG allows an exercise tracing to be interpreted, provided the patient can achieve an adequate workload.
**Exercise stress testing is a suitable first test. Dipyridamole perfusion imaging can also assess inducible ischemia and is the alternative when adequate exercise is impractical.**

**A. Coronary CT angiography.** This depicts coronary anatomy. He can exercise and has an interpretable resting ECG, so exercise testing can relate his symptoms to workload and electrical changes.
**B. Invasive coronary angiography.** Direct angiography is appropriate for selected high-risk patients or refractory symptoms when revascularization is an option. The vignette describes stable symptoms without a prior functional assessment.
**C. Exercise stress testing.** Record symptoms, ST changes, exercise duration and the blood-pressure response. His history of climbing stairs supports trying an exercise protocol.
**D. Dipyridamole perfusion imaging.** This functional alternative uses pharmacologic vasodilation to reveal differences in myocardial perfusion. It is especially useful when exercise stress would be inadequate.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, ch. 74, pp. 1137–1139, Figure 74-5.
Key note: Both C and D received credit. Hazzard favors exercise testing for someone able to exercise with an interpretable resting ECG and describes pharmacologic stress for patients who cannot exercise adequately.
